faqs.q: Who earns more in India, a data analyst or a data scientist?
faqs.a: Data scientists usually earn more than data analysts with similar experience, because the role needs advanced programming, statistics and machine learning skills. Actual pay varies a lot with the company, city, industry and your experience, so compare current job listings for the roles you are targeting.

faqs.q: Can a commerce or arts graduate become a data analyst?
faqs.a: Yes. Many employers hiring data analysts care more about skills than about your degree, especially Excel, SQL, a visualisation tool such as Power BI or Tableau, and basic statistics. Building a few portfolio projects with real datasets is a good way to show these skills. Data scientist roles more often expect a strong maths or programming background.

faqs.q: Do data analysts need to know coding?
faqs.a: Some coding is usually expected, mainly SQL to pull and filter data from databases. Python or R is increasingly useful for analysts and is required in many job descriptions, but data analysts generally need less programming depth than data scientists, who build machine learning models and write production code.

faqs.q: How can a data analyst move into a data scientist role?
faqs.a: Build on your analyst experience by learning Python, deeper statistics and machine learning, then apply them to projects such as forecasting or classification problems with real data. Taking on modelling tasks in your current job, if possible, and showing results in a portfolio makes the switch easier, since many data scientists start out as analysts.
